subject: Biology
title: The Cambrian Explosion
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Cambrian Explosion.

hook.text: For 3 billion years, life was simple. Then, in just 20 million years, nearly every animal phylum appeared.

buildup.text: The Cambrian explosion, 540 million years ago, produced the ancestors of all modern animal groups.

discovery.text: The Burgess Shale fossils reveal bizarre creatures—five-eyed Opabinia, armored Anomalocaris—unlike anything today.

twist.text: What triggered it? Rising oxygen, new genes like Hox, and an evolutionary arms race of predators and prey.

climax.text: In evolutionary terms, 20 million years is a blink. Body plans that took billions of years appeared almost overnight.

punchline.text: Life waited 3 billion years, then exploded.

quiz.question: What happened during the Cambrian explosion?
options: Nearly every major animal phylum appeared rapidly

details.summary: The Cambrian explosion was a burst of animal diversification about 541 million years ago when most major animal body plans appeared in the fossil record within roughly 20 million years. It produced the ancestors of nearly every modern animal phylum from arthropods to chordates.
details.whyItMatters: The Cambrian explosion remains one of the biggest puzzles in evolutionary biology. It challenges gradualist expectations by showing that animal diversity can arise with explosive speed, possibly driven by ecological and genetic revolutions.
takeaways: Most major animal phyla appeared within about 20 million years in the Cambrian
The Burgess Shale preserves bizarre Cambrian animals like Anomalocaris and Hallucigenia
Predation, oxygen rise, and Hox genes likely combined to drive the explosion

faq.question: What caused the Cambrian explosion?
faq.answer: Likely a combination of rising oxygen levels enabling larger body sizes, evolution of eyes triggering predator-prey arms races, and Hox gene duplication allowing new body plan development. No single cause adequately explains the scale and speed of diversification.

faq.question: Was the Cambrian explosion really sudden?
faq.answer: Twenty million years seems instantaneous in geological time but is enormous by human standards. Molecular evidence suggests animal lineages diverged earlier in the Precambrian, so the explosion may partly reflect improved fossil preservation rather than truly sudden evolution.
